endorsements.quote: Methods of addressing it could include technical work aimed at allowing a P4 to compute and express its degree of confidence.

These confidence intervals along with additional information concerning the functioning, strengths, and weaknesses of LLMs in general and P4s in particular, could be provided to surrogates and clinical decision-makers.

Better yet, experimental methods drawn from the cognitive sciences could be used to probe public attitudes and intuitions while systematically varying and testing candidate factors that might be expected to play a role in shaping their perspectives on these questions (Earp et al. 2020 , 2021 , 2022 ; Lewis, Demaree-Cotton, and Earp 2023 ).

unlisted_practices: Make use of an AI patient preference predictor voluntary, letting individuals decide in advance whether, how, and with what data and priority it is used if they lose decisional capacity.
Honor individuals' requests to exclude specific personal data from AI model fine-tuning.
Implement AI patient preference predictors consistent with existing legal and ethical norms for decision-making for incapacitated persons in the relevant jurisdiction.
Prefer locally hosted models or privacy-protective services and secure storage for fine-tuning on sensitive personal data.
Build prototype P4s and compare their accuracy against human surrogates and population-based predictors before clinical use.
Fine-tune prototype P4s at first only on data that is publicly available or for which informed consent was explicitly obtained.
Test AI preference predictor accuracy across languages and pursue language-specific improvements where needed.
Establish the relative usefulness of different data types for preference prediction and weight training data by medical relevance.
Embed AI preference predictors in shared decision-making with clear protocols for using outputs and handling interpretive uncertainty.
Make AI preference predictors explainable by identifying the statements or behaviors underlying each prediction so health professionals, surrogates, and family can scrutinize them.
Develop preference-prediction technology and its ethical guardrails with the involvement of ethicists, clinicians, AI experts, patients, and the public.
Survey the public and patients about their concerns and wishes regarding AI preference predictors before deployment.

screen.reason: This is a theoretical and ethical proposal/commentary advocating for a Personalized Patient Preference Predictor (P4) using fine-tuned large language models, rather than an empirical evaluation.
